newsitem.title: USA: Alabama governor files $700 mln highway bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Alabama governor files $700 mln highway bond bill.

text.p: Alabama Gov. Fob James has formally introduced a proposal to issue $700 million of Alabama Highway Authority revenue bonds.
His long-awaited bill was filed Tuesday in the House by Rep. Joe Carothers, D-Dothan, and in the Senate by Sen. Tom Butler, D-Madison.
Fob spokesman Alfred Sawyer said it was too early to predict the chances of success.
"We're in the process now of trying to determine how much support there is for it, but we're hopeful," Sawyer said.
The bill would use existing gasoline taxes to pay debt service of about $60 million annually on the 20-year bonds.
The plan allocates $150 million of bond proceeds for resurfacing roads and highways, and another $150 million for bridge repair and replacement.

James' proposal would divide $81.9 million of bond proceeds among the state's 67 counties for local projects. Each would get at least $1 million for local projects, while the 17 large counties that collect the most money in gasoline taxes would receive a greater share.
Jefferson County, which includes Birmingham, would get $6.34 million, Mobile County $3.9 million, Madison County $2.6 million and Montgomery County $2.3 million.

The remaining $318 million would finance construction of bypasses around Birmingham, Huntsville, Tuscaloosa, Decatur, Montgomery and Anniston; plus widening of several two-lane highways to four lanes, and various other studies and improvements for roads and bridges.
The projects are listed in the bill, but it does not specify how much would be alloted for each.
